title: Core concepts — accuracy & output quality — P1

terms.definition: Reliability of a language or machine-learning model evaluated in isolation on fixed inputs, without tools, memory, or session context. Covers repeated-run variance, paraphrase sensitivity, and confidence alignment at the inference boundary only.
terms.scopeNote: Use when the evaluation subject is the model component, not the full agent or system.
terms.literatureNote: Core charter vocabulary. Aligns with Princeton HAL where noted in Princeton HAL and related literature; qualifiers apply for infrastructure and BFT senses.

terms.definition: The accuracy observed in deployment after infrastructure faults, stale data, retries, and recovery mechanisms have acted on the system. Can be lower than design-time or benchmark accuracy even when agent logic is correct.
terms.scopeNote: Links outcome measurement to operational conditions. Separate from the analytical definition of accuracy on a clean run.
terms.literatureNote: AAIF term for accuracy after corrections and retries in production. Not widely standardised; captures enterprise 'did we eventually get it right'.

terms.definition: The degree to which an agent's outcome, side effects, and stated understanding align with the declared user intent, agent goal, or multi-agent intent for the scenario — including constraints and success criteria not repeated in the last user message.
terms.scopeNote: WHAT dimension: measures alignment to objective, not whether the procedure was acceptable (see process accuracy and skill adherence). Distinct from task accuracy when rubrics are narrow but user intent was broader.
terms.literatureNote: Implicit in contextual correctness and task completion literature; AAIF names it explicitly for WHAT/HOW evaluation design.

terms.definition: The degree to which an agent's trajectory and outputs follow the instructions, tool allow-lists, and success criteria of the skill package declared in scope for the task.
terms.scopeNote: HOW dimension when evaluation pins a specific skill. Only meaningful when the evaluation envelope names which skill was loaded; otherwise use process accuracy or functional correctness.
terms.literatureNote: Emerges from modular skill frameworks; AAIF links skill artefacts to measurable HOW adherence for audit and attribution.
